notes: §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR4 (as Amendment 2 left it): "The ALPHABET clause provides a means for relating a name to a specified character code set and/or collating sequence", by STANDARD-1, STANDARD-2, NATIVE, implementor-name-2 or the literal phrase, whose subitems order the specified characters as written, put the unspecified ones after them in native order, run a THROUGH pair in either direction and give an ALSO group one position. SpecialNamesBinder.AlphabetBind binds the five phrases at every edition: the three keyword sets as the identity sequence, an implementor-name through AlphabetCodeName (ASCII, EBCDIC), and the literal phrase through AlphabetLiteralPhrase and CollatingTable.Build, which implement subitems 1 to 6 as written; CodedCharacterSet.CharAt gives the code-set ordinal (an ALSO group answers literal-1; the unspecified ordinals are DOC-A.1-186). The phrases 1985 lacks are refused at --std 85 by VisitAlphabetClause (FOR, LOCALE, UCS-4, UTF-8, UTF-16: COBOL0900, probed). Item d, "If the literal phrase is specified, the alphabet-name may not be referenced in a CODE-SET clause", holds because BindCodeSetClause refuses every alphabet whose CodedCharacterSet.Medium is NotProvided, which is every literal-phrase alphabet (COBOL1672 at every edition, worded as the processor's non-support, not as the 1985 rule). Probed at 85: a literal alphabet with a multi-character literal, ordinals, ascending and descending THROUGH, a three-way ALSO and unspecified characters as PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE (18 relations right) and as SORT COLLATING SEQUENCE; EBCDIC, STANDARD-1, STANDARD-2 and NATIVE as SORT sequences; SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS IN each; CODE-SET accepted for the four non-literal phrases (EBCDIC translates the file) and refused for three literal alphabets. The CLASS clause's IN phrase, a 2002 reference to an alphabet that compiles at 85, is the finding of 1985-GR-VI.4.5.4-10. The witness runs a two-character literal alphabet as the program collating sequence.

next.reason: Amendment 2 (X3.23b-1993, pages VI-15 and VI-16) made the literal phrase define a code set too: 'The character code set and/or collating sequence identified is that defined according to the following rules', a new subitem 4 ('the implementor defines the ordinal number within the character code set being specified for each character within the native character set that is not specified by the literal-1 phrase') and THROUGH characters 'are each assigned a successive ascending collating position in the collating sequence being specified and/or a successive ascending ordinal number in the character code set being specified' (§1985:VI.4.5.4 GR4). §2023:12.3.7.4 GR7 carries the rule: the same contexts (NOTE 2, Table 6), NATIVE, the implementor's code-name and k) 'When literal-phrase is specified, the coded character set and collating sequence are defined according to the following rules' with the same subitems 1 to 6, the amendment's subitem 4 verbatim. Three differences remain. (1) 1985 d: 'If the literal phrase is specified, the alphabet-name may not be referenced in a CODE-SET clause'; 2023 has no such refusal: Table 6 reads '| literal phrase | Y | Y |' and §2023:13.18.13.3 SR1 asks only that 'Alphabet-name-1 shall reference an alphabet that defines an alphanumeric coded character set', so a CODE-SET naming a literal-phrase alphabet, refused in 1985, is accepted. (2) 1985 a: 'If the STANDARD-2 phrase is specified, the character code set identified is the International Reference Version of the ISO 7-bit code'; 2023 c): 'the implementor shall specify whether the International Reference Version or a national version is referenced' (made implementor-defined), and STANDARD-1 moves from 'American National Standard X3.4-1977' to 'ISO/IEC 646 International Reference Version'. (3) 2023 k) 5 keeps the unamended THROUGH wording, 'is assigned a successive ascending position in the collating sequence being specified', without the amendment's code-set ordinal, and k) 6 adds 'Literal-1 is the first character in the sequence of multiple characters defined at that ordinal position'. LOCALE, UCS-4, UTF-8, UTF-16 and the NATIONAL phrase are 2023 syntax the 1985 format lacks.
